chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who falls ill, and the month of Ramadan arrives for him, and it passes while he is still sick, and he does not recover until another month of Ramadan arrives. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give charity for the first [one], and fast the second. So if he recovered in between, and did not fast until another month of Ramadan arrived, he should fast both of them together, and give charity for the first one.'

key_terms.صَامَهُمَا جَمِيعاً: he fasts both of them together

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up a missed fast if the illness lasts until the next Ramadan?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the specific scenario of 'ta'arud al-shahrayn' (consecutive Ramadans) for the chronically ill, distinguishing between those who recover within the interval and those who do not. Shia jurisprudence emphasizes that fidya is required for the missed day even when making it up in the subsequent year, reflecting the principle that the obligation of compensation persists until the fast is fulfilled. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the Shia view that fidya and qada can coexist for a single missed day under these conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding

the man who is sick, so he sees a Month of Ramazan and it exits from him and he is sick and does not get well until he sees another Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should give in charity for the first, and he should Fast the second. So if he was well in what is between the two and did not Fast until he saw another Month of Ramazan, he should Fast both of them together, and he should give charity for the first one’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about

a man who is ill. The month of Ramadan comes and he remains ill until the next month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said, ‘He pays charity for the first month of Ramadan and fasts the second month of Ramadan. If in between he had become well but did not fast until the next month of Ramadan, he fasts for both and pays charity for the first month of Ramadan.’”
